legacy_b002: Today I'm only selling. Usual prices. Nothing else.
legacy_b005: Then don't take them. It's not as if this is the only shop I can go to.
legacy_b006: *She puts the goods away, her hand resting on the bag strap, and does not leave at once*
The detective's started on Mother's case. He says what he finds may be bigger than I expect.
Big enough that knowing the truth won't be enough.
Even if we find out who did this to her — getting her out takes connections. Getting back upstairs takes capital. I have neither.
...Don't answer that. I didn't come here to tell you any of this.
legacy_b008: I take back what I said that day. Once we know the truth, I'll help you.
You said I'd have to obey you. And not just in business. I heard you.
You did. I was wrong to say it.
And putting it nicely makes those terms disappear?
Those terms are gone. You can turn down today's offer and keep investigating.
She watches you, then sets her bag down again. Her hand stays on the strap.
I can't repay a loan. I won't take charity.
Then work here. Inspect goods, keep accounts, run errands. I'll help with what you can't manage alone.
We'll find out one thing at a time. I'll tell you when I can't.
...Tell me about the work first. Don't think I've forgotten what you said.
legacy_b011: Then we'll try it this way. I'll do the work. I'll also watch what happens to your promises.
Don't start ordering me about already. I haven't seen you deliver yet.
Bring the detective's findings here first.
...That I can do. I've been looking for somewhere to sort out what he finds.
She shoulders her bag. She doesn't turn at the doorway this time. A few steps outside, she slows.
legacy_b012: ...You'd better not be doing this just to see whether I'd agree.
No. I was thinking too far ahead again.
That actually sounded human this time.
If the investigator finds anything, I'll still come.
legacy_b013: I was wrong that day. Arrange the investigation yourself. Come to me if you need anything.
...At least you know how to apologize first.
Fine. That's the end of it. From now on, say what you mean. Don't make me guess what 'listen to me' was supposed to include.
Mm. If the investigator finds anything, I'll come.
m11_b001: There. Eight hundred for the detective to investigate Mother's case. All of it.
I've counted it three times! Eight hundred. Every last credit.
That used to be just a line on a bill. Now, point to any part of it and I can tell you how I earned it.
Including that lump you insisted wasn't scrap?
The materials inside it sold. You don't have to like it, but show some respect for its contribution.
m11_b002: I've got the money for the detective to investigate Mother's case. Another shop took the rest, and the odd-job people agreed to an advance.
What about the next few days?
I'll keep working. Advancing the pay doesn't make the work do itself.
m11_b003: I sold the locket too. Stop staring at my neckline. I'm still getting used to it myself.
Do you know who bought it?
Yes. Mother comes first. Don't let me being sentimental hold everything else up.
m11_b004: The investigator starts tomorrow. He agreed to check the work records first, rather than question people at the company.
After he finds out who did this to her. What then?
Then we... take it to court.
Will the court look at it?
*Her fingers go still on the stack of money.*
I don't know. I can't even get into the Upper Level. I can't afford a lawyer, and I don't know anyone who still answers my calls.
All I know is that we investigate first. Once we know the truth, there has to be a next step.
m11_b006: I can help with what comes next.
You could work here. Inspect goods, keep accounts, run errands. I'll help work out what to do about the case.
...Do you need someone, or are you inventing a reason for me to take your money?
There's work. And I'll still tell you if it isn't done properly.
I can clean a counter. I'm learning the goods. How far can your help actually go?
We'll need to check the paperwork and find the right people. I've dealt with that in business. I won't promise what I can't secure.
I don't want to hear that something will turn up. I can say that myself.
Then one thing at a time. Judge the results.
She looks down at the money she earned, pressing her thumb over the crease in the top note.
I'll hear the terms. Don't change your manner if I turn them down.
You can keep bringing goods as usual.
m11_b007: First, the term. You help me return to the Upper Level; I work here. Under my own name, not in a seat someone keeps empty for me.
Right. They must want me there because I'm good at the work. Not because of whose daughter I am.
And my investigation, other jobs and mother's affairs keep their time. I'll tell you if something comes up. I can't drop everything when you call.
We'll arrange the shop work ahead.
Mother and the research aren't part of this agreement. Who gets the drive and what course we take must be discussed separately.
Discussed together! Not you deciding first and then informing me.
...One more thing. You have not already decided what I am supposed to call you, have you?
Work first. What you call me is up to you.
I will. If I think you're making me pay with myself, I'll leave. We can agree on work. Don't start adding anything else.
m11_b008: I have a term too. *You set another stack beside hers.* Eight hundred. Wages in advance.
I said I don't want a handout—
It isn't a handout. It's pay. Your mother will need medicine and somewhere to live when she's out. A payment before you start. Shop policy.
...You certainly know how to word things.
I'm paying the investigator myself. I earned that money. Nobody takes that away from me.
m11_b011: She separates the two piles. The detective's goes into an old envelope. She picks up your money, then puts it back on the counter.
Set my work days first. If there's news about mother, I have to go.
See the detective tomorrow. Bring the news back, then we'll arrange it.
This money...is for her medicine and somewhere to live. Not because I failed to raise the investigation fee.
Only then does she put your money away separately. Her fingers pause on the clasp.
I won't shirk the work. Don't let your side stay a promise.
m11_b012: Let's leave it. Follow your own plan for the investigation.
...You'd better not be testing whether I'd take the money.
Not that far ahead. You just have an infuriating way of saying things.
If there's news tomorrow, I'll still come by.
m12_b001: The detective found something. I read it all night. There are still things I can't make out.
I took a detour and changed the meeting place. You're not the only one who knows to be careful.
Sit down. Lay out what you're unsure about.
m12_b002: The drive was hidden in Mother's old laboratory. The investigator couldn't open it. There's a password.
My birthday. She always said that way she wouldn't forget. I've told her so many times not to use it as a password.
m12_b003: She found a way to make ordinary Nutrifruit produce seeds again. Plant it, harvest it, and keep seeds for the next crop.
So people wouldn't have to buy from Pastel every time.
There are records ordering her to stop the trials. Then her access was revoked. And then... the charge.
She never embezzled anything. She just touched the business they least wanted anyone touching.
This gives us a motive. Getting them to release her will take something else.
I know. But for once, I have more than 'my mother wouldn't do that.'
m12_b006: Leave the drive here for now. I can watch the counter. Safer than carrying it from job to job.
Keeping it is one thing. I decide who gets it.
Put it on this receipt. Take it back whenever you come for it.
She reads the receipt, looks at your hand resting on the counter, then slowly lets go of the drive.
m12_b007: Keep it on you. If someone asks here, I'll deal with them first.
You're putting your shop in front of it?
They know you come here. Another shop won't erase that.
Tell me as soon as anyone comes. Don't make a deal and then expect me to follow it.
m12_b008: Also, you've mixed several little components together. One of the labels has fallen off.
You spent so long picking through my goods last time. I wasn't only standing there being angry.
Separate them, then. Anything you're unsure about, leave for me.
m12_b009: She sorts the small parts, hesitates over one, then places it in front of you.
This casing was replaced. The price on the label hasn't changed.
Check inside too. A replaced casing doesn't mean it's broken.
I didn't say it was broken.
Then don't put it with the broken ones yet.
She looks at the pile, takes the part back and places it under the light again.
...Explain how to check. I'll do it myself next time.
m13_b001: Boss, you've been getting close to Eleanor lately. The girl from the Upper Level.
m13_b002: Then you should understand I'm not here on my own account.
m13_b003: She's got a data drive. Hand it over first. Someone will tell her where to collect her mother, alive in the Lower Level.
Deliver first, then wait for your address?
Who else will you check with? Keep delaying and her mother might not last.
Who arranges the release, and when do we see her? Come back with that in writing.
Three hundred if it works. You're a shopkeeper. Don't shut out your own payment.
Write that down too. She needs to know what you're paying me to do.
They say she works for you now. Your word carries more weight than ours.
Then pass it on quickly. Her mother can't wait.
m13_b006: *He glances behind the counter* It's not here?
I've got everything here. Just not what you're looking for.
m13_b007: Her name and yours will both be on the record. Think about that.
So will the message you brought.
m13_b008: Don't keep me waiting too long. My patience isn't that good.
m14_b001: What do we start with today? Those things you mentioned—
Sit down first. Someone from the black market came by. About your mother and that research disk.
m14_b002: You write down the man's words in order for her, including the three hundred credits.
The drive first, then they tell me where to collect her. ...At least they're willing to talk.
Do you know whether this man can arrange her release?
I can ask. If I can meet someone who'll act—
With the drive, or with this paper?
...Do you think I stop listening the moment I'm frightened?
I'm worried that once you're there, only they can change the meeting. They take the drive, and you're still waiting for their next word.
She folds away the line saying drive first, then opens it again. Her fingertip stays on it.
What can I do now? Will sitting here get mother out?
Check where she's held, who handles the paperwork and where she can be seen. Leave the original here. Every question you ask still leaves you a way back.
I have her medication records. The person collecting it signed. I know the name.
...I'll do that. If all I get is wait again, we'll need another way.
m14_b003: There are channels for a protected transfer. We submit material they can act on, confirm who takes responsibility, then discuss publication.
I'll find her medication records. I have her identification too. I know what can't be left out.
m14_b004: I don't have connections that can guarantee her safety. Negotiating an exchange is safer for now.
Then don't pretend it's arranged just to make me feel better. I'd rather hear the truth.
m14_b005: You promised me an Upper Level. Right now I just want to see her.
This comes first. I'll tell you exactly how far we get.
...Don't just tell me not to worry. I'm afraid I really will sit and wait on those words.
When we have something, we lay it out here and check it.
All right. This time, we'll try your way.
m14_b007: Your mother first. We return the research, but verify the release papers and collection point before handing it over.
All right. I won't gamble with her life.
If she asks later, I'll explain. You don't have to carry this decision alone.
m14_b008: We apply for protection first. Once she's safe, we deal with the research. If protection falls through, we go back to the exchange.
Understood. We don't count unconfirmed things as done.
That's what you said about my goods: if you haven't checked it, don't add it to the price.
m14_b009: We could publish it now. But without protection, they may kill her. I cannot promise I can save her.
She tightens her grip on the bag holding the drive, then slowly loosens it, without handing it over.
They will not even say where they would release her. Once I hand it over, all I have is their word. But publishing it now puts her at risk too...
I want her alive. And after everything she has endured, I want her work to survive too.
m14_b010: ...Send the research to the newspaper. At least they will not be able to take that copy back.
You will not wait for news of protection?
No. I do not know whether Mother would agree. This is my decision.
But do not tell me she will certainly be all right. I would believe you.
m14_b011: I've decided. I'll leave the investigation, and our agreement ends here too.
The drive is yours. I can't promise anything about what comes next.
You promised me an Upper Level.
I know. That's why I'm saying it now, before I make a mess of it.
*She puts the drive away and says nothing for a long time*
...Good. At least you didn't pretend you could carry it.
m14_b013: Leave the shop work today. Write down what you need to ask, then rest.
I can't cancel tomorrow's job. I'll bring the papers, but later.
...I thought you were going to tell me to follow your arrangements again.
I remember. Good that you do too.
m15_b001: I've brought the paperwork for getting Mother out. Checked every page. The dates match too.
Put them here. Have you eaten?
That's what you said last time.
m15_b002: The name on the medication record checks out. But they changed the collection point.
Halfway. Then I came back. He said I wouldn't meet the next person without the drive.
She puts down the creased record. Its corner has gone soft under her fingers.
I nearly went. You can say you told me so.
You brought it back. We can still negotiate.
I found the original official. He'll let me check the release papers without going through that messenger.
Record the name, time and place separately. Once the official confirms, we arrange delivery.
...Go through it with me again. Especially the two steps he said we could skip.
m15_b003: I have the protection documents. They haven't confirmed who's taking over. I thought of sending the research first, to avoid another delay.
Once it's sent, who will wait for that confirmation on your behalf?
...Deliver first, then wait for someone else to speak. Again.
Medication on top. I'll check the channel; you check who's taking over. It isn't done until both match.
I copied the medicine she can't miss separately. If they can't answer that, a notice won't reassure me.
m15_b004: We can't count the protection as arranged. We have no confirmed transfer for today.
The papers are ready, and it's still no?
Which is why we can't send the research first. We use the fallback: exchange it for her release, after checking the papers.
...I don't like this plan. But telling me now is better than leaving me waiting for something that hasn't happened.
m15_b005: She takes wrapped food from her bag and sets it beside the papers. She starts pushing it towards you, then stops.
Bought an extra portion. Pay for it normally. Don't say you'll add it to my wages.
...Never mind. Eat first. I need this space to finish sorting the papers.
m15_b006: She points out a date. Only after you've checked does she put a small tick beside it.
...I need you to look before I count on the next step. Just today.
m16_b001: I saw mother. At the place we checked. The official hadn't changed either.
Yes. I saw her first, checked her medicine and the papers, then handed over the drive.
The messenger tried to lead me somewhere else again. I didn't follow. In the end he had to step aside.
You held them to what you'd checked.
...If I'd gone straight there with the drive, I wouldn't even have known whom to ask where she was.
She asked how much weight I'd lost. I'd prepared so much to say. That one question undid all of it.
m16_b002: They sent someone to the shop with those three hundred credits.
Sent them straight back. They wanted me to push you into handing over the drive. I did not work for them, so I will not take their money.
She looks at you for a moment. Slowly, the tension leaves her shoulders.
m16_b003: Mother's been transferred safely. I saw her. The person taking over went through every medicine with me.
None. When the application notice came first, I wanted to push you to send the research.
Then I checked and found they hadn't set the transfer time. If I'd sent it then...
Because you made me look at the notice again. ...I'll remember this time.
She complained my writing was too small. Nobody else would start with that.
Settle her first, then handle the research as agreed.
m16_b004: I meant to come in, explain the paperwork properly, then discuss what comes next.
m16_b005: She comes around the counter and stops. You open your arms. At last she leans into you, forehead against your shoulder. She tries to speak, but her breathing breaks first.
All the way back, I kept thinking what to tell you first.
m16_b006: Don't repeat what just happened to anyone.
Go be with her. There's no work for you here today.
Come if you want. Sort out those sleeves first. They nearly swept something off the counter last time.
...I know. I'll have the clothes altered myself. Don't order anything for me first.
I'll ask Wilde about a home. You and your mother need somewhere lasting.
She's out now. You're still taking care of the rest?
Getting her out wasn't all I promised.
...I'll go home first. We'll talk about tomorrow, tomorrow.
m12_b004: Before the drive, there's something else. When that man pretending to be your uncle brought the box, I saw something was wrong. I didn't warn you.
Her hand stops at her bag. She pushes the half-withdrawn papers back inside.
Yes. I should have told you then.
I kept wondering whether I couldn't see anything for myself. You were here watching.
And after one apology, I'm supposed to take out the drive and follow your arrangements?
No. You can take it away.
...Next time there's danger, tell me first, however ugly it is. I'll decide what I can handle.
m12_b005: I'll keep the drive. We can discuss what comes next. The shop agreement ends here.
Then remember that. Don't take it back someday.
m16_b007: And the box. I haven't forgotten.
This time you told me who came, what they said, which steps hadn't worked.
More than once I wanted to blame you for delaying. Then I could only come back and ask you to check.
...Next time there's danger, tell me first. Don't wait for me to ask.
